messages:
Ana (support): FYI — Customer 'BrightPay' opened a high-priority ticket: sudden 200-400ms tail latency and increased errors for requests originating in eu-central-1. They say responses are coming from us-west-2.

Maria (customer-success): Customer says their app started degrading ~08:12 UTC, only for traffic from their EU users. Screenshots and curl example attached.

Ana (support): Repro steps from customer: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -H "X-Request-Region: eu-central-1" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate` -> response has header `x-redwood-serving-region: us-west-2` and 250ms extra RTT.

Priya (oncall): @Jorge can you check routing tables/policies? I see a spike on cross-region egress from us-west->eu in metrics.

Jorge (sre): Looking. Initial glance: global routing service showed increased fallback count to primary 'cost-optimized' pool around 08:10. Investigating whether geo DB lookup failed and policy fell back.

Sam (eng-platform): What changed in routing policy recently? I didn't deploy anything to prod today. Will check PRs.

Jorge (sre): Dumps from the router at 08:11: `route_eval(client_region=eu-central-1) -> candidate_pools: [eu-standard, eu-burst], resolved: us-west-cost-opt` -> WAT.

Ana (support): Customer logs with `x-request-id=rp-7f3b` attached. They got 502s intermittently and high p99 latency.

Priya (oncall): @Sam please flip the routing flag to prefer latency over cost for region selection in the fallback policy, temporarily, to stop further impact.

Sam (eng-platform): Flipped flag `fallback.priority=latency` at 08:22 UTC; propagation to edge routers in ~15s.

IncidentBot: :information_source: deploybot reported config-change `fallback.priority` by sam at 08:22 UTC.

Maria (customer-success): After the flag flip customer reports latency back to normal and no more wrong-region headers. They confirmed at 08:30. :white_check_mark:

Jorge (sre): Root-cause hypothesis: the geo-IP DB was failing for a small percentage of requests (cache TTL misconfigured during last update), so region resolver returned NULL and the selection logic used fallback pool ranking which mistakenly preferred a cheaper us-west pool. Looking at logs, geo-lookup errors spiked at 08:09.

Sam (eng-platform): I found a config drift: when we rolled the geo-db refresh job last week, TTL default was set to 0 for the edge caches for some instances. That allowed momentary misses under load. I patched the job to set ttl=300s and redeployed the refresh job at 08:40.

Priya (oncall): Mitigations performed: 1) temporary fallback.priority change at 08:22, 2) geo-db refresh job patched and redeployed 08:40, 3) added alert on geo-lookup-error-rate > 0.5% to paging channel.

Ana (support): Customer-impact summary for ticket: BrightPay experienced elevated latency and intermittent 502s for EU-origin traffic from 08:09–08:30 UTC. Root cause: geo-IP cache TTL drift causing region resolver misses -> wrong fallback selection. Action items queued.

Jorge (sre): Action items (assigned): - Sam: fix geo-db deploy script to enforce TTL and add unit test (due EOD). - Priya: add paging alert for geo-lookup-error-rate and runbook (due tomorrow). - Ana/Maria: outreach to BrightPay with timeline + apology + mitigation summary (draft by EOD).

Sam (eng-platform): Will also add a canary check in the routing eval that rejects candidate pools with mismatched geo tags; PR forthcoming.

Maria (customer-success): I'll include a note about credits for impacted window; want legal signoff first.

Ana (support): Prelim postmortem notes: cause: stale/zero TTL on geo-db edge cache causing resolver misses. Immediate fix: priority toggle and geo-db job patch. Long-term: enforce TTL in CI, add routing canary, and add alerting.

Priya (oncall): I'll schedule a 30-min blameless sync later to convert notes into a short incident postmortem doc and assign owners.

Jorge (sre): Logs and traces uploaded to S3 at `s3://redwood-incidents/1772456789-geo-routing-eu/` for forensics.

Ana (support): Closing the Slack thread for now. Will update when postmortem draft is live. :thumbsup:
